summary: Apple's Translation framework translates text between a language pair on device, through a system translation popover, a session API and language-availability checks. BifrOSt has a popover model and presenter (presentation, language-pair check, result and replacement), session and language-availability types over installed phrase-table packs, but no neural translation engine and no drawn translation UI in the shell. Its locale and spellcheck code only localize strings, format numbers and dates, and check spelling in the same language.

gaps: Translation sessions run only over installed phrase-table packs (sdk translation.rs, TranslationSession); there is no neural engine (see the last gap).
The translation popover presenter is in the SDK (sdk translation_popover.rs), but the shell does not draw it, and no inline translate action exists.
Locale data covers only en and is, so even the related localization layer lacks the language pairs a translation feature would need (docs/bifrost-ui.md, Locale gaps).
No neural translation engine: no Argos or bergamot style model is in the Arch repositories, so only the phrase-table language packs (LanguagePack) exist
